text: Given valid placeholder credential headers, When the agent calls initialize then tools/list, Then all 17 watchguard_* tools are returned with the documented names, and tools/call watchguard_get_account (mocked 200) returns the account payload, not an error envelope

Given no accountId argument and no X-WatchGuard-Account-Id header, When watchguard_get_account is called, Then it resolves to the credential owner's own account and never substitutes any other account id

Given any one of X-WatchGuard-Access-Id / X-WatchGuard-Password / X-WatchGuard-Api-Key is missing, When any watchguard_* tool is called, Then the server returns HTTP 401 whose body names exactly the header that was omitted, with no fallback to environment variables

Given X-WatchGuard-Account-Id is set to a managed account id, When a tool is called, Then the client calls POST /v1/audiences before POST /oauth/token, and the resulting token request includes the returned audience value

Given mocked vendor responses of 404 / 429 / 500, When a tool call hits each, Then the result is the structured envelope with code not_found / rate_limited / upstream_error respectively, and 429/500 are retried at least once (honoring Retry-After on 429) before the final envelope is returned

Given watchguard_delete_account or watchguard_delete_operator is called without the required id argument, When invoked, Then it is rejected with an invalid_argument envelope (no wildcard/all form exists), and both tools' schema marks destructiveHint true

Given a mocked operator create response carrying a transaction_id, When the tool returns, Then the result includes that transaction_id, and watchguard_get_operator_transaction_status called with it returns the mocked final status

Given two concurrent requests carrying different X-WatchGuard-* credentials, When their tool calls interleave, Then neither request ever reads the other's ContextVar-held credentials, and there is no module-level or global cache of tokens or account data

Given a real WatchGuard Cloud account, When live calls are made to watchguard_get_account, watchguard_activate_device, and watchguard_create_operator, Then each returns live vendor data matching the documented response shapes
steps: Obtain a real WatchGuard Cloud account's Access Id, Password, and Api Key (Manage Access page)
Set X-WatchGuard-Access-Id / X-WatchGuard-Password / X-WatchGuard-Api-Key on the request
Call watchguard_get_account with no accountId argument
Call watchguard_activate_device with a real activation key (only against a vendor test/trial account, never assumed to exist)
Call watchguard_create_operator with a disposable test operator
expect: Each call returns a 200-shaped tool result matching the documented WatchGuard response fields, not an error envelope
evidence: No WatchGuard Cloud test/trial account is available to this pipeline; not a blocker for publishing to INT per SOP 'no test account is not a blocker' and mcp-track.md section 3 completion criteria. Listed in the dev report as 'needs a real vendor account'.
